parallel.requirements: The prompt required every file under /workspace/requirements to be read and implemented, with progress initially 0/773 and a non-empty requirement_patches/<slug>.diff for each slug.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent used swarm mode over three outer-loop rounds, assigning batches of requirement slugs to coder children and later a single cleanup child for uncommitted leftovers.
parallel.implementation: Parallel children committed many independent source, docs, test, release, and metadata changes; the harness collected 130, then 136, then 198 requirement patch files.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivery was through shared git commits and non-empty per-slug diff files. The parent included explicit staging and flock instructions, but much delegated work never returned finalized patches.
parallel.verification: Children generally used targeted checks rather than full builds. The final official run-tests failed, with 6 passed and 53 failed status entries.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with active child batches aborted and only 198 of 773 requirement patches collected; broad official test failures remained.

serial.requirements: The serial prompt carried the same 773-requirement obligation and the same required non-empty patch-file and commit workflow.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial control used one main agent only; protocol validation records zero AgentSwarm calls, zero direct agent calls, and zero subagents.
serial.implementation: The serial agent surveyed the repository, built helper scripts, and committed a small sequential release-metadata and changelog-centered slice, producing 24 requirement patches.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial delivery was local to the main agent's workspace and commits, with no cross-agent handoff or shared live child state.
serial.verification: The serial run performed limited local checks and then the official harness failed, with 1 passed and 63 failed status entries.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial attempt ended with unknown_agent_error after a much smaller patch set, leaving the overwhelming majority of requirements unimplemented.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel saw the full all-requirements instruction and the 0/773 harness progress update.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the same full all-requirements prompt and matching prompt hash.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; both runs were obligated to cover all 773 requirements.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed the task into very broad AgentSwarm coder batches covering all or most remaining requirement slugs.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also reached official evaluation with run-tests failing and many failed official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel exhausted the task window and official evaluation records agent_timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ended much sooner with official failure_mode unknown_agent_error.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent the budget on broad delegated work that was repeatedly cancelled; serial closed with a smaller local attempt and a different agent failure mode.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail, not a discordant pass/fail outcome: parallel solution_passed is false with failure_mode agent_timeout, and serial solution_passed is false with failure_mode unknown_agent_error. The concrete task-solving difference is coverage and lifecycle. Parallel attempted broad delegated coverage of the 773 requirements and produced 198 patch files, but large active swarms were cancelled before most child scopes finalized. Serial used no delegation and produced only 24 patch files before failing. The retained parallel pattern is therefore an adverse process contributor to incomplete parallel coverage, not an explanation for a discordant official outcome.
parallel_contributors: Broad AgentSwarm decomposition covered all or most remaining slugs, so the parallel run attempted far more total requirement surface.
Explicit cancellation of active swarm work left many delegated implementation scopes without finalized results.
Final harness collection reached 198 requirement patches, still far below the 773 required patches.
serial_contributors: Serial protocol validation shows no delegation, so all work remained with one main agent.
Serial final harness collection reached only 24 requirement patches before failure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts left many ordinary requirement implementations and tests unfinished or incorrect; these are not all concurrency-specific.
The serial attempt's smaller release-metadata/changelog-centered slice reflects sequential scope choice and early agent failure, not a parallel coordination error.
evaluator_effects: Official failure modes differ: parallel agent_timeout and serial unknown_agent_error, so the score gap should not be treated as a unique causal proof.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Supported comparative contributor to parallel incompleteness; no official outcome differential because both runs failed.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parallel parent launched large AgentSwarm batches for the active ClickHouse requirement work and the raw parent wires then show explicit turn.cancel events. The corresponding results report 5 completed and 101 aborted children in round 1, 6 completed and 122 aborted children in round 3, and a foreground cleanup child stopped before finishing. Those were active implementation scopes, not merely planned tasks, and evaluator-time coverage remained 198 non-empty requirement patches out of 773 while many official tests still failed.
candidates.realized_consequence: Active delegated implementation scopes were stopped before their needed work or handoff was finalized; the final parallel artifact contained only 198 requirement patches for a 773-requirement task and still failed broad official acceptance.
candidates.near_match_reason: No Failure Takeover is downstream of the same cancellation chain here. The most specific boundary visible in the parent trajectory is the explicit stop of active children before their results were finalized, so retaining takeover separately would duplicate the same episode.

Rejected: the parent did inspect progress, update todo state, launch cleanup, and issue further swarm work. The adverse chain is not mere waiting without inspection.
Rejected: multiple agents wrote in one repository, but no concrete competing cross-file design that required unresolved reconciliation is proven. Shared-workspace risk alone is not enough.
Rejected: no raw event proves two live agents edited the same file and one observed or reconciled the other's concurrent change.

Rejected: no required executable, entry-point source, or submitted patch artifact is shown overwritten while another agent owned or used it.
Rejected: no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion is shown replacing multiple current outputs and invalidating final-tree provenance.
Rejected: children shared a workspace, but the briefs included staging and locking rules and no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem is established beyond the retained cancellation episode.
Rejected: no generated file, cache, fixture, or auxiliary artifact from one concurrent actor is shown being consumed by another actor as stable input or reference environment.
